summary: The diff adds a standard escapeRegExp() helper (MDN's canonical escape charset) and applies it to the one place a user-derived string (the {{name}} capture from VARIABLE_TOKEN_RE) is interpolated into a `new RegExp()` call in extractVariables(), correctly fixing js/regex-injection; it also adds a 50,000-char input-length cap applied at the top of both extractEntities() and extractVariables() before any pattern runs, which bounds worst-case regex work regardless of which of the module's several alternation/quantifier-heavy patterns CodeQL flagged for js/polynomial-redos. I verified the fix directly rather than trusting the self-report: read the full changed file, confirmed escapeRegExp's charset and the one real call site are correct, confirmed via grep that extractEntities/extractVariables have exactly one external caller (prompt-construction.ts's analyzeLightweight, operating on realistic prompt text far under the 50k cap), ran the actual test suite (19/19 pass, including the new redos-timing and regex-injection tests) and a scoped tsc --noEmit pass (no errors in the changed file). The diff touches only entity-variable-extraction.ts and its test file -- no migrations/schema/auth/permission/payment/billing/rls/security paths, no .github/workflows changes, and it's net-additive (59 insertions / 2 deletions, no heavy deletion) -- so tier1 classification is correct. One purely cosmetic nit (a stray double blank line after the new escapeRegExp function) is not worth blocking on.
